model_annotation: The line chart illustrates the percentage of employed individuals ("Anteil Erwerbstätige in %") across different age groups ("Alter") for four distinct population groups in Germany: those without a migration background (black line), those born in Germany (gray line), those who migrated before 2009 (light blue line), and those who migrated since 2010 (dark blue line). The x-axis represents age, ranging from 20 to 70 years, with tick marks at 5-year intervals. The y-axis represents the employment rate in percent, ranging from 0% to 100%, with major gridlines at 20% intervals. The black line (without migration background) starts at approximately 60% at age 20, rises to a plateau near 85% between ages 30 and 55, then declines sharply to below 10% by age 70. The gray line (born in Germany) follows a similar pattern but with more fluctuations, starting near 55%, peaking around 85%, and falling to about 15% at age 70. The light blue line (migrated before 2009) begins around 35%, rises to about 70%, and then gradually declines to 10% by age 70. The dark blue line (migrated since 2010) starts at approximately 38%, fluctuates between 40% and 65% until age 60, then drops steeply to near 0% by age 70, with a notable spike to 25% at age 68 before falling again. All lines show a general decline in employment rates after age 60, with the most recent migrant group exhibiting the most volatile pattern in older age groups.
